chunks: And Al-Husayn ibn Saeed wrote to Abu Al-Hasan Al-Ridha (peace be upon him), asking him: Regarding the bier of the deceased being carried, is there a specific side that should be started with in carrying from its four sides, or whatever is lightest for the man carrying it from whichever side he wishes? So he (peace be upon him) wrote:

key_terms.سَرِيرِ الْمَيِّتِ: Bier or stretcher for carrying the deceased

ai.seo_question: Which side of the bier should be carried first when transporting a deceased person?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih*, Imam Ali al-Ridha (peace be upon him) clarifies the flexibility of funeral rites by ruling that there is no obligatory starting side for carrying the bier, allowing the carrier to choose based on ease. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle of *al-asl fi al-ashya' al-ibahah* (the default state of things is permissibility) in matters not explicitly detailed by the Prophet, emphasizing practicality over rigid formalism in burial customs.
